summary: A worker laid off after years at one employer is much less likely to be working again by the next year if he or she is past fifty-five.
realLife: The Bureau of Labor Statistics found about two-thirds of long-tenured displaced workers had work again by January 2026, but only about 57 percent of those aged 55 to 64 and about 39 percent of those 65 and older.
sources: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Worker Displacement news release: https://www.bls.gov/news.release/disp.nr0.htm
inGame: job-ended event plus a job record; age on the person. Reemployment is read from whether a new job record appears.

turns.summary: The older worker stops looking and treats the layoff as the end of working life.
pulledBy: a spouse who is still working
turns.writesBack: job record closed; mood: relieved or restless; journal note

turns.summary: An old coworker at another firm hires the older worker within months.
pulledBy: good standing at the old employer
turns.writesBack: new job record; coworker tie closer

turns.summary: Months pass without an offer and the household budget tightens.
turns.writesBack: mood: worn; tie to spouse strained; journal note
